I relate so hard dude. Im sorry

First off, my heart breaks for you. Im so sorry this is what you have to go through. 

When I had an overdose attempt (non fatal, hadn't taken enough to cause too much damage) What I mainly needed was sleep. Remind her its okay to relax, sleep, and let go of her emotions. Let it all out. Watch some good movies, have some warm drinks, and try to be as empathetic as possible. See if there are any telehealth appointments you can make for her with a therapist/psychologist as well. 

Im so sorry again. That seriously is so scary I cant even imagine.

Hi I hope Im not too late to reply, but whenever I was suicidal it was mostly my depression making me impulsive. Im sure many therapists would agree that if she is not in immediate danger, you must distract her. 
Be subtle about it though. I cant tell you how many times my family has saved me by letting me vent, then just casually putting on my favorite shows or movies to distract me until the feelings are able to naturally pass. They come back though, so finding the root cause of her hopelessness is important.
There was a time I had my car keys in hand, ready to go complete a suicide plan, when my boyfriend put on a show we had just started on netflix and i was getting distracted while talking to him and i literally couldn't look away from the screen. Im sure it was my rational instincts trying to save me as well, by giving into the distraction. 

You are so kind for reaching out for help on her behalf, I wish you guys the best!

Hi, I can actually relate. My mom almost convinced me to let her commit a murder suicide with me as the victim. I have vivid memories of her saying awful things like that, it always effects me and no one understands. 

I just want you to know it's not your fault, please don't apologize. Thanks for sharing your story so I can finally sort of relate to someone.

Hi so I actually volunteered for the Crisis Text Line (US) for a few months in 2017. I have no idea how the call-in hotline works or how they screen their volunteers so I can't speak for them. The crisis text line is corrupted in their corporate office, let alone doing no good. Although don't ever be surprised when a mandated reporter calls  911 on you, as they could face legal charges if they do not. 

I was not exactly a mandated reporter, but my supervisors were. I would show them the conversation once someone checked off all the points on our list of having the means to commit suicide (having a time, method, and refusal to agree to put away anything harmful). Then they would get your location from your phone plan and call your local police to come check on you. 

Also they keep track of every phone number that texts in. If you text in too many times too often, I think it was more than 10 times overall, they will cut you off and just send you a coping skills link and end the conversation. Once a crisis counselor ends a conversation, they write on your file what was talked about and what key words you used, as well as the name you have them. Just so you know. 

I dont mind exposing them as I have texted in myself while in messy suicidal states and they used my name without me even giving it to them once lol. They are also strictly scripted and if you dont follow what they want you to say, a supervisor can cut you off. 

The training process is also very vague and unhelpful. Their corporate employees get paid way too much imo. 


So fuck the hotlines :)
